ai.title: Remove middle-out compression from SDK llm.ts
ai.summary: Removed `transforms: ['middle-out']` from `getProviderOptions` in `sdk/src/impl/llm.ts`. This change addresses potential toolcall/toolresult pairing mismatches caused by the compression. Scope limited to SDK LLM implementation.

eli5.text: The SDK's LLM implementation no longer applies 'middle-out' compression when fetching provider options, resolving potential mismatches between tool calls and their corresponding results. Developers building on this SDK will see more reliable tool result pairing during LLM interactions, as the previous compression technique could interfere with proper call-result alignment. This is a minor, behind-the-scenes adjustment affecting how the SDK handles API communication with language models.

ai.title: Fix thinking preview truncation
ai.summary: Removed `Math.min(..., 120)` width cap and adjusted `effectiveWidth` to subtract ellipsis prefix length in `cli/src/components/thinking.tsx`. Changed `wrapMode` from `word` to `none` and line joiner from space to newline. Ensures 3-line thinking preview renders accurately without premature truncation or wrapping artifacts.

eli5.text: You may have noticed the assistant's thinking preview sometimes appeared cut off or awkwardly wrapped while you were interacting with the CLI. The team removed an unnecessary 120-character width limit and fixed how line breaks are handled, so the three-line thinking preview now displays fully and cleanly without premature truncation or wrapping artifacts. This applies to anyone running the CLI tool today.

ai.title: Context pruner token counting fix
ai.summary: Context pruner token counting now accurately includes all message fields when images or media are present. The previous logic only counted specific metadata keys (role, toolCallId, toolName) for tool messages and just role for user/assistant messages, ignoring other fields. The updated implementation destructures the message to count all non-content fields via `countTokensJson(rest)`, ensuring tags and other metadata contribute to the token estimate. This change affects internal context management within `.agents/context-pruner.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant is deciding how much of a conversation to keep in memory, it now counts every part of a message, including hidden tags and labels, not just the visible text and a few basic details. This affects anyone whose conversations include images or tool results, since those messages were previously under-counted and could be trimmed incorrectly. You wouldn't notice this directly, but your conversation history will be managed a bit more fairly behind the scenes.

ai.title: Context pruner preserves important tools
ai.summary: Context pruning logic updated to preserve essential tool calls (read_files, write_todos, etc.) and recent messages. Large tool results are truncated based on a 1000-char threshold, and aggressive pruning targets 25% of max tokens. Non-important tool pairs outside the last 30 messages are removed. Changes confined to .agents/context-pruner.ts.

eli5.text: When the assistant works on a long task, it sometimes needs to tidy up its memory to make room for new thoughts. The cleanup process now protects the most important actions, like reading files, updating task lists, and writing changes, so those aren't accidentally discarded. Large outputs from tools are trimmed automatically, and older, less important tool interactions are removed first. If you were watching, the assistant would keep working on your task without losing track of the files it's editing or the steps it's following.

ai.title: Context pruner removes all but last instructions prompt
ai.summary: Added PASS 0.5 to context-pruner.ts to filter out all but the last INSTRUCTIONS_PROMPT message. This prevents context bloat from repeated instruction prompts in long sessions. The change is internal to the .agents/ subsystem and affects message history construction before tool result truncation.

eli5.text: If you keep a long chat going with an agent, the system used to repeat the same opening instructions over and over as it built up the message history, making each turn bulkier than necessary. Now the agent trims away all but the most recent copy of those instructions before deciding what to cut next, so conversations stay leaner. This is a behind-the-scenes cleanup inside the agent tooling (the internal.agents subsystem) and is live today. If you never inspect the full message history yourself, you won't see it change anything obvious.

ai.title: Fix types in context-pruner tests
ai.summary: Updated `context-pruner.test.ts` to fix TypeScript errors. Changed `mockAgentState` declarations from `as AgentState` to `: any` to allow partial objects. Added optional `maxContextLength` parameter to `runHandleSteps` helper to pass params correctly to `handleSteps`.

eli5.text: The people who build and check the assistant's memory management tool fixed a few mistakes in their test files. They adjusted how the test data is set up so it doesn't get confused by strict checking rules, and they made one of their test helpers accept an extra setting so it can pass along the right configuration. If you looked at the test files, the setup objects would look slightly different, but the actual tool that helps the assistant remember things works the same way as before.

ai.title: Fix orphan tool result in agent runtime
ai.summary: Tool execution errors now emit `onResponseChunk` with `type: 'error'` instead of pushing synthetic `ToolMessage` objects to `toolResults`. This prevents orphaned tool results from appearing in the conversation history when a tool call fails validation or execution. The change applies to both `executeToolCall` and `executeCustomToolCall` in `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/tool-executor.ts`, removing the `jsonToolResult` dependency for error paths.

eli5.text: When an AI tries to use one of its tools and that tool fails, the assistant now reports the failure directly as an error message instead of stuffing a fake tool reply into the conversation history. This stops confusing, orphaned messages from appearing in the chat log when something goes wrong. You'd notice fewer broken or duplicated entries in the conversation when a tool call errors out, and the system is live today.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI 1.0.564 ships block preservation and pruner fixes
ai.summary: The CLI package version advanced from 1.0.563 to 1.0.564 in cli/release/package.json. This release bundles 10 updates: chat blocks are now preserved on CLI error paths in message-updater.ts, OpenRouter error logging now captures full message history, middle-out compression was removed from SDK llm.ts getProviderOptions, the CLI thinking preview component truncates accurately without width caps, the context pruner counts all non-content message fields via countTokensJson, preserves important tool calls and recent messages with a 1000-char truncation threshold, filters duplicate INSTRUCTIONS_PROMPT messages in PASS 0.5, fixes context-pruner test TypeScript declarations to allow partial objects, and tool-execution errors emit onResponseChunk type error instead of orphaned ToolMessage objects in executeToolCall and executeCustomToolCall. The agent-runtime tool executor error path no longer depends on jsonToolResult, preventing synthetic tool results from polluting conversation history.
ai.evidence: cli/release/package.json version field: 1.0.563 → 1.0.564. Release updates: 2025-12-29 (preserve chat blocks on CLI error, include message history in OpenRouter error log, send-message test expects blocks), 2025-12-30 (remove middle-out compression from SDK llm.ts, fix thinking preview truncation in thinking.tsx, context-pruner token counting fix and important-tools preservation, instructions-prompt filter, fixed context-pruner test types, fix orphan tool result in agent-runtime

eli5.text: This update makes your chats more reliable and your screen previews more accurate. You will no longer lose your conversation context when a tool call fails, and long thinking summaries will display on three lines instead of getting cut off weirdly. The system now keeps important actions in memory during long conversations instead of trimming everything, so you won't lose track of what the assistant was doing. Error messages also now include more helpful details from your chat history, so if something goes wrong, you get better information about what happened. Upgrading means fewer surprises and clearer visibility into what your assistant is thinking.

ai.title: Switch web analytics init to Next.js instrumentation hook
ai.summary: Replaced `web/src/lib/server-init.ts` with `web/instrumentation.ts` to use Next.js native server lifecycle for `initAnalytics`. Removes manual `server-only` guard and layout import, relying on `register()` to run once at startup. Added `path: false` to `next.config.mjs` webpack fallbacks to resolve bundling issues with `pino`/`thread-stream`.

eli5.text: The website has switched to using Next.js's native startup hook to initialize analytics, replacing the old manual initialization code. This means analytics will now start automatically when the server boots, without needing to import and run it from a separate file during layout setup. The change also added a webpack fallback for the 'path' module to fix bundling issues with logging libraries. This is a behind-the-scenes refactor that should make analytics initialization more reliable, particularly in ensuring PostHog events are not missing.

If you visited the site today, you wouldn't see them appear anywhere yet; they're now stored and ready for the website to use them in places like browser tabs or app icons. This is a behind-the-scenes addition that makes the logos available for developers to reference, but it doesn't change what visitors see right now.

ai.title: Add debug logging to web instrumentation
ai.summary: Added console logs to `web/src/instrumentation.ts` `register()` to trace analytics initialization. Logs capture environment variables (`NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT`, PostHog keys) and success/failure states. Internal only; no user-facing behavior change.

eli5.text: When the company's main website starts up, it now quietly prints a few diagnostic messages that reveal which environment it is running in (such as development or production) and whether the keys needed for its analytics service are present. These messages appear only in server-side logs and never show up for people browsing the site, so nothing about your experience changes. If someone with access to those logs opens them, they will see simple notes confirming whether the analytics setup step ran successfully or failed.

ai.title: CLI process cleanup handlers replace manual renderer destroy
ai.summary: installProcessCleanupHandlers in cli/src/utils/renderer-cleanup.ts registers SIGTERM, SIGHUP, SIGINT, beforeExit, exit, uncaughtException, and unhandledRejection listeners to destroy the renderer. This replaces scattered cleanupRenderer() calls in cli/src/hooks/use-exit-handler.ts, cli/src/hooks/use-login-keyboard-handlers.ts, and cli/src/components/project-picker-screen.tsx. The change ensures terminal state resets on all exit paths, including crashes and unhandled rejections, not just explicit Ctrl+C or exit handler flows. SIGKILL remains uncapturable per POSIX constraints.

eli5.text: When the assistant closes down, it now reliably resets your terminal so the text doesn't get garbled left behind. Instead of cleaning up only in a few specific places (like when you press Ctrl+C), the reset now happens automatically on every possible way the program can stop, including crashes and sudden system requests. You'd notice because your terminal should look clean and normal again after the program exits, no matter how it ended. One signal (SIGKILL) can never be caught, so that case is left as-is per system rules.

ai.title: CLI release bumped to 1.0.565
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI package version advanced from 1.0.564 to 1.0.565 via a single-line edit to the "version" field in cli/release/package.json. This is a routine release increment in the same-day commit sequence, capturing the day's prior CLI and web improvements, and ships as a version-bump-only artifact with no lockfiles or code changes. The release packages the preceding web analytics instrumentation migration, logo assets, debug logging, and process cleanup handler changes alongside earlier model and context-pruning fixes.
ai.evidence: Commit 859b4283 bumps the "version" field in cli/release/package.json from "1.0.564" to "1.0.565" (diff hunk shows the single-line version change in freebuff/cli release package manifest).

eli5.text: This release focuses on making the Freebuff web experience and CLI terminal app more reliable and easier to maintain. Web analytics now initialize through Next.js native startup hooks, which fixes bundling errors that could affect tracking and removes the need for manual analytics guards. The web app also gains new logo icon assets for static serving, improving visual branding consistency. The CLI terminal now installs automatic process cleanup handlers that reliably reset the terminal display on every exit path, including crashes, unhandled errors, and system interrupts like Ctrl+C, replacing scattered manual cleanup calls. Upgrading gives users a more stable terminal that always cleans up properly when closing, and a smoother web experience with more robust analytics initialization and branding.

ai.title: writetodos tool result replaced with static message
ai.summary: The write_todos tool result schema and handler now return a static message string instead of echoing the input todos array. This prevents duplication of todo data in tool outputs. Changes applied to common/src/tools/params/tool/write-todos.ts and packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/tool/write-todos.ts.

eli5.text: When you use the assistant to keep a running list of todos, the confirmation you get back no longer repeats the entire list of tasks you just wrote. The assistant now simply acknowledges that your todos were written, so the list isn't duplicated in the conversation. You can still manage your todos exactly as before; you'll just see a shorter, cleaner confirmation each time you save them.

ai.title: Replace console logs with structured logger in analytics init and chat
ai.summary: Replaced raw console.log calls with structured logger.info calls in web/src/instrumentation.ts and added debug logging for analytics initialization in common/src/analytics.ts and chat completions requests in web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts. This change standardizes log output format for production debugging, ensuring analytics configuration details and request metadata are captured consistently alongside existing event tracking. Scope limited to web server instrumentation and common analytics initialization logic. Note that sensitive API keys are logged as boolean presence flags rather than raw values to prevent secret leakage.

eli5.text: When the system starts up and when someone sends a chat request, it now writes down what's happening in a neater, consistent format instead of scattered plain text notes. This means the team can more easily look back and figure out why something went wrong, and they can see whether important setup values (like whether an analytics connection is configured) are present without exposing any private keys. There is nothing you would notice directly as a user; this just makes the system quieter to run and easier to debug behind the scenes.
